### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>fallow-rs/fallow (fallow)</summary>

###
[`v3.36.0`](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#3360---2026-10-24)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/compare/v3.35.0...v3.36.0)

##### Added

- **Built-in dotenv CLI plugin support.** `fallow migrate` now maps the
`dotenv` plugin key. Scripts invoking `dotenvx` credit
`@dotenvx/dotenvx`,
  and `dotenvx run -- <command>` credits the wrapped command, as
  `varlock run --` already does. Thanks
[@​VariableVince](https://redirect.github.com/VariableVince) for
the patch in
[#​3771](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/pull/3771).
(Closes
[#​3762](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3762))

- **Experimental tsrs backend for type-aware analysis.** Set
`FALLOW_TYPE_AWARE_BACKEND=tsrs` to run the semantic pass on
[tsrs](https://redirect.github.com/oxc-project/tsrs), the Rust port of
the TypeScript 7 checker, instead of TypeScript-Go. Install the pinned
`tsrs` version next to `fallow-type-aware`. `fallow type-aware status`
and `_meta.type_aware` report the backend that ran. TypeScript-Go stays
the default.

- **`health.cyclomaticPolicy: "literal-membership"` counts a literal
  membership chain as one predicate.** A chain such as
  `kind === "a" || kind === "b" || kind === "c"` then adds no cyclomatic
  increments for its `||` operators. Only strict equality checks of one
  identifier against string, number, bigint, boolean, or `null` literals
qualify. The policy applies to the `maxCyclomatic` gate and to every
CRAP
score. Findings report the policy value as `cyclomatic` and the standard
  value as `standard_cyclomatic`, the summary names the policy, and
  `--complexity-breakdown` marks the chain operators with
  `literal_membership`. The default stays `standard`. The health score,
complexity density, and hotspots keep the standard count. The parse
cache
  version changes because the cached breakdown has the new flag.
(Closes
[#​3781](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3781))

- **Fallow reports config entries that match something but change
nothing in the dead-code run.** Three new kinds in
`workspace_diagnostics[].kind` carry these entries, each with the config
entry in `pattern`:

- `entry-pattern-redundant`: an `entry` pattern whose matched files are
all runtime entry points from another source, for example `package.json`
fields and scripts, a plugin, an infrastructure config or
`dynamicallyLoaded`.
- `ignore-dependencies-entry-redundant`: an `ignoreDependencies` entry
that hid no dependency finding. A glob that matches no declared
dependency keeps the `ignore-dependencies-glob-unmatched` kind and is
not reported twice.
- `ignore-patterns-entry-redundant`: an `ignorePatterns` glob that
excluded no file that a built-in ignore, `.gitignore` or the file type
filter does not already skip. A glob for build output has an effect only
after a build, and the message says so.

The entries reach JSON, SARIF `toolConfigurationNotifications[]`, the
stderr note in human, compact, CodeClimate and `github-annotations`, and
the LSP information diagnostic on the config entry. Markdown,
`github-summary`, the PR comments and the review summary add a separate
`Redundant config entries` section after `Unmatched config patterns`. A
`--production` run reports none of the three kinds, because that run
checks fewer files and dependency sections. No exit code changes, and no
`schema_version` changes, because `workspace_diagnostics[].kind` is an
open set.
(Closes
[#​3824](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3824))

##### Changed

- **Every platform npm package now ships a `LICENSE` file and a full
README.**
  This covers the `@fallow-cli/<platform>` CLI binaries, the
  `@fallow-cli/fallow-similar-code-<platform>` sidecar binaries, the
`@fallow-cli/fallow-node-<platform>` addons and
`@fallow-cli/fallow-node`.
The README names the platform and the package to install instead, and
says
how the binary is verified. The `fallow-similar-code` platform packages
now
  also have a description.

- **A file that nests too deep to parse has its own workspace
diagnostic.** Fallow does not parse a file that nests brackets past the
parser cap, or that needs more stack than fallow reserves. Such a file
was reported as `source-parse-degraded`, with a message about parser
errors, although the file can be valid code. It is now reported as
`source-nesting-too-deep`, with the cap in `limit`. The message says
that `fallow fix` holds back its actions while the file is reachable,
and that `ignoreFindings` takes a generated file out of the run. The
file still counts for the `parse-error` gate, and its item in
`gate_outcomes["parse-error"].files` carries the new optional `reason:
"nesting-too-deep"`. The human report, the GitHub Action and the GitLab
template name that reason instead of "1 parser error".
`workspace_diagnostics[].kind` is an open set, so no schema version
changes, but a consumer that filters on `source-parse-degraded` must
also match `source-nesting-too-deep` to keep seeing these files.

- **Fallow now parses with Oxc 0.155 and converts coverage with
`oxc_coverage_instrument` 0.17.0.**
  A short TypeScript input that made the parser use seconds of time and
gigabytes of memory
([oxc-project/oxc#27637](https://redirect.github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27637))
now stops at its syntax error at
once. Analysis output for real projects does not change. A string with a
  lone surrogate now keeps it as `\uXXXX`, so the extraction, graph and
duplication caches get a new version and the first run after the upgrade
  is cold. Oxc 0.155 needs Rust 1.97, so the minimum Rust version of the
  Fallow crates goes from 1.96 to 1.97.

- **The agent gate prints a short block message.** When the gate that
  `fallow agent install` and `fallow hooks install --target agent` write
blocks a `git commit` or `git push`, stderr now holds one line for each
finding that caused the block, the verdict, and the path of the full
JSON
  report. Under the default `gate = "new-only"` the list holds only the
introduced findings, so inherited findings no longer fill the context of
  the agent. The full report goes to `.fallow/gate-report.json` in the
  audited tree. Set `FALLOW_GATE_REPORT` to write it to another path, or
`FALLOW_GATE_OUTPUT=json` to print the full report on stderr as before.
The exit codes do not change. Run `fallow agent install` again to update
an
installed gate. Thanks
[@​ankoor7](https://redirect.github.com/ankoor7) for the report.
(Closes
[#​3725](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3725))

##### Fixed

- **`fallow dead-code --type-aware` no longer confirms a used class
member or
export as unused when a shorthand name reads it.** The type-aware check
now
  finds a class member that a shorthand destructure reads, for example
  `const { run } = service`, `({ run }: Service) => run()` or
`({ run } = service)`, and a renamed assignment destructure, for example
`({ run: local } = service)`. It also finds an export that a shorthand
object
property reads, for example `{ value }`, and an export that a
destructure of
a namespace import reads, for example `const { value } = ns`. Before
this
  fix, a used member that only a parameter destructure or an assignment
  destructure read could get a guarded `remove-class-member` fix. For an
  array or loop assignment destructure, and for a nested assignment
  destructure with a default value, the check now abstains with
  `dynamic-member-access`.

- **`fallow health` counts runtime code in modules that export only
types.**
Top-level calls, assignments, `await`, and runtime declarations keep a
module
in coverage gaps. Pure type and ambient declarations remain excluded.
The
extraction cache version is bumped so warm caches pick up the new facts.
Thanks
[@​xiaofeilovecoding](https://redirect.github.com/xiaofeilovecoding)
for the
patch in
[#​3578](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/pull/3578).
(Closes
[#​3549](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3549))

- **`unused-class-members` credits members that a parameter destructure
or a destructuring assignment reads.** Without `--type-aware`, `({ m }:
Service) => m()` and `({ m } = service)` did not credit `Service.m`, so
Fallow reported a used member as unused. Fallow now credits these reads
in the same way as `const { m } = service`. The parameter form works for
arrow functions, function declarations and methods, with renamed keys,
defaults and nested type literals such as `({ svc: { m } }: { svc:
Service })`. A rest element still marks the whole class as used.

- **The GitHub Action no longer fails `command: audit` on a default
shallow checkout.** On a `pull_request` event, a depth-1 checkout of the
merge commit has no merge base with the PR base, so `fallow audit
--changed-since` exited 2 with "no merge base". The Action now fetches
the smallest history that gives a merge base: the base commit, then the
parents of the merge commit, then a bounded deepen. A failed fetch does
not fail the job. `fetch-depth: 0` stays the recommended setup.

- **The napi-rs plugin finds a generated loader in a subdirectory.** A
build with `napi build --cwd binding` writes the loader to
`binding/index.cjs`, but the `napi` config stays in the package
manifest. Fallow read only the package directory, so it reported each
platform package of the loader as an unlisted dependency. Fallow now
also reads the direct subdirectories of the package, except
`node_modules`, `target`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, hidden directories,
and directories with more than 32 script files. The WASI workers and
`browser.js` next to such a loader count as generated too.

- **CI scripts named outside a `run` value are no longer unused files.**
Fallow now reads three more GitHub Actions forms. A step that runs only
`${{ matrix.<path> }}` runs the values of that key path in the matrix of
its job. An `actions/github-script` step loads the files after
`${process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/` or `${{ github.workspace }}/`, and
the files of `require('./path')`. A step `env` entry whose whole value
is `${{ github.action_path }}` or another workspace anchor makes
`"$NAME/script.mjs"` resolve like that anchor.

- **`fallow dead-code` no longer reports the dependencies of a
gitignored workspace member.** A pnpm workspace can declare a directory
that CI fills with a clone of an upstream repository, for example `vite`
or `rolldown`. Source discovery does not read the files of a gitignored
member, so the run cannot prove that its dependencies are unused. The
member stays a workspace for imports and catalog references.

- **A `workspace:<name>@<range>` dependency alias resolves to the
aliased workspace package.** With `"vite": "workspace:@scope/core@*"`,
an import of `vite/pack` resolves through the `exports` map of
`@scope/core`. Before, a workspace member with the name `vite` took the
import, and the import was unresolved when that member had no `./pack`
export.

- **`unused-class-members` credits members that a nested destructure
reads.** Without `--type-aware`, `({ k: { m } } = { k: service })`, `({
k: { m } } = holder)` and `({ k: { m } = service } = {})` did not credit
`Service.m`, so Fallow reported a used member as unused. The `const`
forms had the same gap. Fallow now follows a nested pattern into an
object literal property, a default value and a static member path. The
member path form reads `holder.k.m` in the same way as the member
expression, so it credits a member only when Fallow knows the class of
`holder.k`.

- **`fallow dead-code --type-aware` no longer confirms an export as
unused when
a namespace object can read it.** The type-aware check now credits an
export
  that a static read of a namespace object reads, for example
  `({ value } = ns)`, `const { "value": local } = ns`,
  `function run({ value } = ns)`, `(ns as typeof ns).value`,
  `outer.inner.value` after `export * as inner`, and `m.value` after
`import m = require("./values")`. When the check cannot prove which
exports
a namespace use reads, for example `console.log(ns)`, `const copy = ns`,
  `export { ns }`, `const { ...rest } = ns`, `ns[key]` or
  `module.exports = require("./values")`, it now abstains with
`dynamic-behavior` for every export of that module, also the exports
that a
  barrel re-exports. A destructure that can read a nested namespace, for
example `const { inner } = outer`, abstains for the exports of the
nested
  module. A dynamic import, for example `import("./barrel")`, now also
abstains for the exports that the barrel re-exports. Before this fix,
such an
  export could get a `confirmed-no-static-references` decision.

- **`fallow dead-code --type-aware` abstains for a class member that a
computed
  destructure key can read.** `const { [key]: run } = service` and
  `({ [key]: run } = service)` now give `dynamic-member-access`, as
  `service[key]` already did. A string key, for example
  `const { "run": local } = service`, now credits the member.

- **tsconfig `paths` aliases that point into `node_modules` no longer
become unlisted dependencies.** A `paths` entry such as
`"@components/*": ["./node_modules/some-theme/src/components/*"]` made
Fallow report `@components/shared` as an unlisted dependency, because
Fallow credited the specifier text and not the package that the alias
resolves into. Fallow now treats each specifier that a `paths` pattern
of the nearest tsconfig matches as an alias, as TypeScript does, and
credits the package of the resolved file. This is also true when a real
package has the same name as the pattern. A `paths` entry onto a
declaration file, such as `"react": ["./node_modules/@types/react"]`,
still credits `react`. Without an install, an alias into a package
directory that does not exist credits that package and is not an
unresolved import.

- **A file with deeply nested brackets no longer aborts the run.** A
source with thousands of nested `(`, `[`, `{` or template substitutions
overflowed the parser stack, and the stack overflow killed the whole
`fallow` process. Fallow now measures the nesting before it parses a
file. A file past the limit shows as a file that failed to parse,
`fallow dupes` finds no clones in it, and the analysis of the other
files continues. Brackets inside strings, comments and template text do
not count. The extraction and duplication cache versions change, so the
first run after the upgrade parses every file again. OSS-Fuzz found
this.

- **`unused-class-members` no longer reports a used member as unused
when one of these destructure forms is its only read.** This applies
with and without `--type-aware`. In each example, `Service.m` is now
used:
- A `for...of` destructure, such as `for (const { k: { m } } of [{ k:
service }])`, `for ({ m } of [service])`, `for (const { m } of
services)` with `services: Service[]` or `for (const { m } of
[...services])`.
- A parameter destructure with a default value, such as `function run({
m } = service)` or `function run({ k: { m } } = { k: service })`.
- A parameter annotated with `typeof`, such as `({ k: { m } }: typeof
holder)` or `({ k: { m } }: { k: typeof service })`.
- A getter or a spread in the source object, such as `{ get k() { return
service } }` or `{ ...holder }`.

- **`unused-class-members` no longer credits a class through a local
shadow.** Without `--type-aware`, a module instance `const service = new
Service()` gave credit to `Service.m` for `service.m`, `service['m']`,
`const { m } = service` and `({ m }: typeof service)` inside a function
that declares its own `service`. Fallow then missed an unused member.
Fallow now ignores this credit when the nested `service` provably holds
no class instance: an object literal of functions and primitives, a
primitive or function value, or a parameter whose type annotation is a
primitive, literal or function type. A type literal or a named type
gives no proof, because a class instance can satisfy it. A class
instance that the nested scope declares keeps its credit.
(Closes
[#​3798](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3798))

- **`unused-class-members` no longer reports a used member as unused
when a destructure of an imported instance or of a class field is its
only read.** This applies with and without `--type-aware`. In each
example, `Service.m` is now used:
- A destructure of an instance from another module, such as `const { m }
= service` after `import { service } from './service'`.
- A destructure of a class field, such as `const { m } = this.service`
in a class with `constructor(private service: Service)`.
- The assignment, parameter default and `typeof` forms of these
destructures, such as `({ m } = service)`, `run({ m } = this.service)`
and `({ m }: typeof service) => m()`.

- **`unused-exports` no longer reports the exports of a namespace import
as unused when a destructure with a computed key reads it.** A computed
key, such as `const { [name]: value } = ns`, can read any export, so all
exports of `ns` are now used.

- **The language server and the MCP `decision_surface` tool no longer
abort on nesting that the CLI survives.** Both ran analysis on threads
with a 2 MiB stack, so a deeply nested file overflowed that stack and
stopped the process. The language server now gives its analysis threads
the 16 MiB stack of the CLI workers. Its Tokio runtime uses two worker
threads, because analysis runs on the blocking threads and the Rayon
pool. `decision_surface` and `run_decision_surface` now parse on the
analysis worker pool, as the other tools do. Their thread count now
follows the `threads` option.

- **Deep nesting without brackets no longer aborts a run.** TypeScript
generics, JSX elements, `class extends`, ternaries, arrows, assignment
chains and long member or call chains could overflow the stack, and the
whole process stopped. Each parse of a source file now runs on a stack
that is sized from the length of the file. A file up to about 15 KB
still parses on the analysis worker. A larger file parses on its own
thread with a stack of that size. This applies to every analysis that
parses a file: dead code, duplication, health, similar code, mutation
testing and the config file plugins.

- **Deeply nested arrow functions no longer make extraction quadratic.**
Each function hashed its whole source text for runtime coverage, so a
chain of nested arrows took time that grew with the square of its
length. 160000 levels took about 17 seconds. A function with more than
64 levels of nested functions below it now gets no `source_hash`. Real
code stays far below that, so every real function keeps the same hash.
The coverage inventory also computes columns in linear time for nested
functions on one line, and it no longer sends the hash of empty input
for a span that it cannot read.

- **A very large file no longer parses on a stack that is too small.**
The parse stack cap is now 64 GiB on 64-bit targets, which a source over
64 MB reaches in a release build. A file that needs more stack is
reported as a failed parse, like a file with too deeply nested brackets.
Before, such a file got a capped stack and could stop the run.

- **A deeply nested stylesheet no longer risks a stack overflow in the
CSS parser.** CSS Modules class extraction, `fallow health --css`
analytics and color parsing now check the bracket depth before they call
the CSS parser, and they run the parse on a stack sized for the
stylesheet. A stylesheet past the limit falls back to the plain class
scan, or is left out of the CSS analytics. The depth check now reads a
stylesheet with CSS rules: a `//` inside `url(//host/a.png)`, a CSS
escape or an unquoted `url()` body no longer hides the rest of a
minified file. The extraction cache version changes, so the first run
after the upgrade parses every file again. OSS-Fuzz found this.

- **Bare `fallow` now applies the `coverage-gaps` rule, as `fallow
health` does.** Before, the combined run did not compute coverage gaps,
so a `coverage-gaps` rule at `error` never failed it. Now an enabled
rule shows the gaps in the health section, and a rule at `error` makes
the human run exit 1. The JSON `gate_outcomes` object gets a
`health-coverage-gaps` entry. Like the other findings rules of the
combined run, the machine formats exit 1 on it only with
`--fail-on-issues` or `--ci`. Thanks
[@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the report.
(Closes
[#​3823](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3823))

- **A suppression that only `--production` needs is no longer reported
stale
in a run without `--production`.** Production mode excludes test files.
An
  export that only a test file imports is unused there, so its
`fallow-ignore-next-line unused-export` comment is necessary. A run
without
`--production` credits the test import and does not use the comment.
That
run now keeps the comment out of `stale-suppression` when every
reference to
the export comes from a file that production mode excludes. The comment
stays stale when a package entry that production mode keeps re-exports
the
  export. This applies to `unused-export` and `unused-type`. Thanks
  [@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the report.
(Closes
[#​3825](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3825))

- **Vite projects no longer report Sass files that Vite loads without an
import as unused.**
  Three cases caused false findings. An `@use` in
`css.preprocessorOptions.scss.additionalData` now credits the file that
Sass
loads when the specifier has no extension, leaves out the `_` of a
partial, or
names a directory with an `_index` or `index` file
([#​3819](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3819)).
An `@use` in a Sass
file now resolves through a Vite `resolve.alias` entry, with the Sass
partial
and directory-index rules. Before, Fallow reported the import as
unresolved
and the target partial as unused
([#​3820](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3820)).
The Sass settings file that
`vite-plugin-vuetify` reads from `styles.configFile` is now an entry.
Fallow
reads the path relative to the Vite `root`
([#​3821](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3821)).
Thanks
[@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the three
reports.
(Closes
[#​3819](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3819),
[#​3820](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3820),
[#​3821](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3821))

- **A private class method now takes coverage from its own `#name`
record.**
  Before, `fallow health --coverage` always reported a private method
(`#name() {}`) as `estimated`, also when the coverage data had a record
for
that method. Fallow now uses a record that has the same `#name` near the
method. A record at the exact position of the method is used first. Near
the method, the record must be the only one with that name. Fallow does
not
give a private method the coverage of the function that holds it or of a
  public method. istanbul-lib-instrument writes no record for a private
  method, so its reports do not change.
Thanks [@​Jerc92](https://redirect.github.com/Jerc92) for the
report.
(Refs
[#​3816](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3816))

- **A script that an Nx `run-commands` target runs is no longer reported
as an unused file when `project.json` contains a comment.**
Fallow now reads `project.json` as JSONC, as Nx does. Line comments,
block
comments and trailing commas no longer hide the target commands. Thanks
to
[@​Pajn](https://redirect.github.com/Pajn) for the report and the
clear reproduction.
(Closes
[#​3704](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3704))

- **`fallow audit --gate new-only` no longer reports an unchanged
anonymous function as introduced when only its CRAP score changes.**
When a file has several anonymous functions, audit matches each head
finding to a base finding. Before this fix, a CRAP change from estimated
to measured coverage stopped the unchanged function from matching its
own base finding. The line-order fallback then paired it with a
different, smaller function, and audit reported it as introduced. Audit
now also matches on the cyclomatic and cognitive values without the CRAP
score before it uses line order. The matched pair still compares the
CRAP score. Thanks [@​Jerc92](https://redirect.github.com/Jerc92)
for the report and the reproduction.
(Closes
[#​3815](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3815))

- **A workspace import now keeps its credit when the package `exports`
point into `dist/src/` and the build output exists.** A package with
tsconfig `rootDir: "./"` and `outDir: "./dist"` emits `src/index.ts` as
`dist/src/index.js`. Fallow now uses the `rootDir` and `outDir` of the
package tsconfig to map that output back to `src/index.ts`. Before, the
imported exports were reported as unused after a build. Thanks
[@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the report.
(Closes
[#​3817](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3817))

- **A warm cache now gives the same result as `--no-cache` after the
build output of a workspace package appears or goes away.** The graph
cache key now includes whether each static entry path in the project and
workspace `package.json` files exists on disk. Thanks
[@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the report.
(Closes
[#​3818](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3818))

- **`fallow health --production` no longer marks tested functions as
untested in the CRAP estimate.**
Production mode keeps test files out of the analysis. The static
coverage
estimate used the same file set, so it found no tests. Each function
with a
cyclomatic complexity of 6 or more then failed the default `maxCrap` of
30.
Coverage gaps also reported tested files and exports as untested. Fallow
now
reads test reachability from a graph of the full project, and findings
still
come only from production files. A production run now gives the same
CRAP

Thanks [@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the

when
Node ran every path of the method. Its public twin with the same body
was
measured and had no finding. The V8 converter now writes a record for
each
private method (`#name`, `get #name`, `set #name`) with its own call
count,

Thanks [@​Jerc92](https://redirect.github.com/Jerc92) for the

`.member` that follows a namespace and comes before `(`, and the mixin
name
after `@include`. In `.module.sass` files, the scan also skips the mixin

the
session branch.** A strict `git push` from a linked worktree of the
session
repository also audited the session tree, because linked worktrees share
refs. Untracked build output in the session thus blocked every push from
a
clean worktree. The gate now audits only the worktree when git shows
that
the push cannot send the session branch: the options are only `-u`,
`-q`,
  `--set-upstream`, `--force-with-lease` and `--force-if-includes`, each
  refspec source is the checked-out branch of the worktree and not the
session branch, and a push without a refspec has `push.default` unset or
  `simple`, `current`, `upstream` or `nothing` and no remote `push` or
`mirror` setting. Any other push from a linked worktree, and any git
error
during the check, keeps the session audit. The strict push form now also
accepts `--force-if-includes`. Run `fallow agent install` again to
update an
  installed gate.

- **A CODEOWNERS file with thousands of wildcards no longer stalls
ownership lookups.**
All CODEOWNERS rules match in one automaton, and its lookup time grows
with
  the number of wildcards (`*`, `?`, `[`, `{`). A 4 KB file with one
  `*a*a*a…` pattern took seconds for each lookup. Fallow now rejects a
pattern with more than 32 wildcards, or a file with more than 4096, with
an
error that names the limit. Large public CODEOWNERS files use fewer than
  400\. OSS-Fuzz found this.

- **A CODEOWNERS pattern with an escaped space now parses.**
  GitLab writes a space in a path as `\ `, for example
`/docs/Security\ Release.md @owner`. Before, Fallow split the line at
that
  space, and `--group-by owner` and `--group-by section` failed with
"dangling ''". GitLab's own CODEOWNERS file failed in this way. On
Windows, a
  backslash in a pattern is now an escape, as on other platforms, and no
  longer a path separator. Thus `\ ` and `\#` now work on Windows too.

##### Performance

- **Very long member chains extract much faster.** Extraction built the
dotted name of a member chain again at each link, and each build copied
the name once per link. A file with a chain of 4000 links (`a.b.b.b...`)
took several seconds to extract. Fallow now builds each name in one
pass, so the same file takes a fraction of a second. Real code does not
have chains this long, but generated or hostile input can. The
extraction output does not change.

- **Public API entry resolution no longer resolves every module path
again for each missed package entry.**
A package entry that exists on disk but is not in the module graph, such
as
an extensionless `bin` script, made Fallow resolve the real path of each
module in the package. Fallow did this again for each candidate path
that it
  probed. Fallow now builds the canonical module index one time for each
package and resolves each parent directory one time. On a large project,
  this removes several seconds from `fallow dead-code` and from the
  `--type-aware` refinement. The results do not change.

- **A very long member chain no longer makes extraction slow and
large.** For a chain such as `a.b.b.b` with thousands of links, each
link recorded the full name of its receiver, so the time and the cached
output grew with the square of the chain length. Fallow now records a
receiver name only up to 64 links. A link deeper than that records no
member access. A fluent builder chain such as `new Builder().a().b()`
now records each step name once, so a long chain keeps the credit for
all of its steps, and a chain that repeats a method stays small. The
extraction cache version changes, so the first run after the upgrade
parses every file again. OSS-Fuzz found this.

- **Long member, `await`, `+`, JSX tag and fluent call chains are now
linear
to analyze.** A file with a chain of many thousand links took minutes,
or
used gigabytes of memory, because several path builders copied the whole
  path at each link or scanned a growing list at each step. For example,
  160000 nested `await` took 33 seconds and now take 0.04 seconds, and a
  fluent chain of 4000 calls with different method names used 700 MB. A
fluent chain now gives one fact for the chain instead of one fact for
each
call. A taint source path or a JSX tag receiver longer than 64 links is
not
recorded, the same limit that member access names use. The cache version
  changes, so the first run after the upgrade parses all files again.

- **Long heritage names and long dotted component tags in Astro and MDX
files
are now linear to analyze.** Each level of `interface X extends
a.b.c...` or
`<a.b.c... />` recorded the full name of its receiver, so the time and
the
output grew with the square of the name length. For example, an
interface
heritage name of 20000 links took 110 seconds and now takes 0.08
seconds. A
receiver longer than 64 links is not recorded, the same limit that
member
  access names use. The names of `class C extends a.b.c...` and
`implements A.B.C...` are now built once, instead of a copy of the name
at
each link. The cache version changes, so the first run after the upgrade
  parses all files again.

references.** Before, a class that only a Shopify `.liquid` section
applied was reported as an `unreferenced-css-class`. Fallow now reads
files with the extensions `liquid`, `njk`, `hbs`, `handlebars`, `twig`,
and `blade.php`, and any class-like word in them counts as used.
Templates are more lenient than Markdown: the whole text of a template
counts, so a common word such as `hidden` or `title` in a template also
credits that class, while a Markdown file counts only when it has
dynamic class syntax. A class prefix before a `{{` echo, as in `grid--{{
columns }}`, also counts. `{{` is a shared interpolation marker, so it
also applies to `.vue`, `.html`, `.md` and `.astro` sources with dynamic
class syntax, and these can report fewer classes too. The new top-level
`markupExtensions` key adds other template extensions, for example
`["tpl", "erb"]`. A value that ends in a script, stylesheet, data or
asset extension, such as `module.css` or `d.ts`, is a config error. The
walk honors `.gitignore`, `ignorePatterns` and `--max-file-size`. These
files do not join source discovery, so they never become unused files.

for the report. (Closes
[#​3917](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3917))

retry-confirmed survived mutants to `.fallow/mutation/journal.jsonl`

--resume` reuses these results and runs only the other mutants. A
journal of other inputs exits 2 with `FALLOW_MUTATION_RESUME_MISMATCH`
and names each input that differs. A resumed mutant has `resumed: true`,
and the report has a `resume` object. A complete run removes the

under `--quiet`, that names each failing findings gate and the flag that
enforces it: `[W] Exit code 0: gate error-severity-findings (2 at or

all runtime entry points from another source, for example `package.json`
fields and scripts, a plugin, an infrastructure config or

the LSP information diagnostic on the config entry. Markdown,

`--production` run reports none of the three kinds, because that run
checks fewer files and dependency sections. No exit code changes, and no

- **`fallow dead-code --type-aware` no longer confirms a used class
member or
export as unused when a shorthand name reads it.** The type-aware check
now

  `const { run } = service`, `({ run }: Service) => run()` or
`({ run } = service)`, and a renamed assignment destructure, for example
`({ run: local } = service)`. It also finds an export that a shorthand
object
property reads, for example `{ value }`, and an export that a
destructure of
a namespace import reads, for example `const { value } = ns`. Before
this

  destructure read could get a guarded `remove-class-member` fix. For an
  array or loop assignment destructure, and for a nested assignment
  destructure with a default value, the check now abstains with
  `dynamic-member-access`.

- **`fallow health` counts runtime code in modules that export only
types.**
Top-level calls, assignments, `await`, and runtime declarations keep a
module
in coverage gaps. Pure type and ambient declarations remain excluded.
The
extraction cache version is bumped so warm caches pick up the new facts.

(Closes

or a destructuring assignment reads.** Without `--type-aware`, `({ m }:

Fallow reported a used member as unused. Fallow now credits these reads
in the same way as `const { m } = service`. The parameter form works for
arrow functions, function declarations and methods, with renamed keys,
defaults and nested type literals such as `({ svc: { m } }: { svc:
Service })`. A rest element still marks the whole class as used.

shallow checkout.** On a `pull_request` event, a depth-1 checkout of the
merge commit has no merge base with the PR base, so `fallow audit
--changed-since` exited 2 with "no merge base". The Action now fetches
the smallest history that gives a merge base: the base commit, then the
parents of the merge commit, then a bounded deepen. A failed fetch does
not fail the job. `fetch-depth: 0` stays the recommended setup.

- **The napi-rs plugin finds a generated loader in a subdirectory.** A
build with `napi build --cwd binding` writes the loader to
`binding/index.cjs`, but the `napi` config stays in the package
manifest. Fallow read only the package directory, so it reported each
platform package of the loader as an unlisted dependency. Fallow now
also reads the direct subdirectories of the package, except
`node_modules`, `target`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, hidden directories,
and directories with more than 32 script files. The WASI workers and
`browser.js` next to such a loader count as generated too.

- **CI scripts named outside a `run` value are no longer unused files.**
Fallow now reads three more GitHub Actions forms. A step that runs only
`${{ matrix.<path> }}` runs the values of that key path in the matrix of
its job. An `actions/github-script` step loads the files after
`${process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/` or `${{ github.workspace }}/`, and
the files of `require('./path')`. A step `env` entry whose whole value
is `${{ github.action_path }}` or another workspace anchor makes
`"$NAME/script.mjs"` resolve like that anchor.

- **`fallow dead-code` no longer reports the dependencies of a
gitignored workspace member.** A pnpm workspace can declare a directory
that CI fills with a clone of an upstream repository, for example `vite`
or `rolldown`. Source discovery does not read the files of a gitignored
member, so the run cannot prove that its dependencies are unused. The
member stays a workspace for imports and catalog references.

- **A `workspace:<name>@<range>` dependency alias resolves to the
aliased workspace package.** With `"vite": "workspace:@scope/core@*"`,
an import of `vite/pack` resolves through the `exports` map of
`@scope/core`. Before, a workspace member with the name `vite` took the
import, and the import was unresolved when that member had no `./pack`
export.

- **`unused-class-members` credits members that a nested destructure
reads.** Without `--type-aware`, `({ k: { m } } = { k: service })`, `({
k: { m } } = holder)` and `({ k: { m } = service } = {})` did not credit
`Service.m`, so Fallow reported a used member as unused. The `const`
forms had the same gap. Fallow now follows a nested pattern into an
object literal property, a default value and a static member path. The
member path form reads `holder.k.m` in the same way as the member
expression, so it credits a member only when Fallow knows the class of
`holder.k`.

- **`fallow dead-code --type-aware` no longer confirms an export as
unused when
a namespace object can read it.** The type-aware check now credits an
export
  that a static read of a namespace object reads, for example
  `({ value } = ns)`, `const { "value": local } = ns`,
  `function run({ value } = ns)`, `(ns as typeof ns).value`,
  `outer.inner.value` after `export * as inner`, and `m.value` after
`import m = require("./values")`. When the check cannot prove which
exports
a namespace use reads, for example `console.log(ns)`, `const copy = ns`,
  `export { ns }`, `const { ...rest } = ns`, `ns[key]` or
  `module.exports = require("./values")`, it now abstains with
`dynamic-behavior` for every export of that module, also the exports
that a
  barrel re-exports. A destructure that can read a nested namespace, for
example `const { inner } = outer`, abstains for the exports of the
nested
  module. A dynamic import, for example `import("./barrel")`, now also
abstains for the exports that the barrel re-exports. Before this fix,
such an
  export could get a `confirmed-no-static-references` decision.

- **`fallow dead-code --type-aware` abstains for a class member that a
computed
  destructure key can read.** `const { [key]: run } = service` and
  `({ [key]: run } = service)` now give `dynamic-member-access`, as
  `service[key]` already did. A string key, for example
  `const { "run": local } = service`, now credits the member.

- **tsconfig `paths` aliases that point into `node_modules` no longer
become unlisted dependencies.** A `paths` entry such as
`"@components/*": ["./node_modules/some-theme/src/components/*"]` made
Fallow report `@components/shared` as an unlisted dependency, because
Fallow credited the specifier text and not the package that the alias
resolves into. Fallow now treats each specifier that a `paths` pattern
of the nearest tsconfig matches as an alias, as TypeScript does, and
credits the package of the resolved file. This is also true when a real
package has the same name as the pattern. A `paths` entry onto a
declaration file, such as `"react": ["./node_modules/@types/react"]`,
still credits `react`. Without an install, an alias into a package
directory that does not exist credits that package and is not an
unresolved import.

- **A file with deeply nested brackets no longer aborts the run.** A
source with thousands of nested `(`, `[`, `{` or template substitutions
overflowed the parser stack, and the stack overflow killed the whole
`fallow` process. Fallow now measures the nesting before it parses a
file. A file past the limit shows as a file that failed to parse,
`fallow dupes` finds no clones in it, and the analysis of the other
files continues. Brackets inside strings, comments and template text do
not count. The extraction and duplication cache versions change, so the
first run after the upgrade parses every file again. OSS-Fuzz found
this.

- **`unused-class-members` no longer reports a used member as unused
when one of these destructure forms is its only read.** This applies
with and without `--type-aware`. In each example, `Service.m` is now
used:
- A `for...of` destructure, such as `for (const { k: { m } } of [{ k:
service }])`, `for ({ m } of [service])`, `for (const { m } of
services)` with `services: Service[]` or `for (const { m } of
[...services])`.
- A parameter destructure with a default value, such as `function run({
m } = service)` or `function run({ k: { m } } = { k: service })`.
- A parameter annotated with `typeof`, such as `({ k: { m } }: typeof
holder)` or `({ k: { m } }: { k: typeof service })`.
- A getter or a spread in the source object, such as `{ get k() { return
service } }` or `{ ...holder }`.

- **`unused-class-members` no longer credits a class through a local
shadow.** Without `--type-aware`, a module instance `const service = new
Service()` gave credit to `Service.m` for `service.m`, `service['m']`,
`const { m } = service` and `({ m }: typeof service)` inside a function
that declares its own `service`. Fallow then missed an unused member.
Fallow now ignores this credit when the nested `service` provably holds
no class instance: an object literal of functions and primitives, a
primitive or function value, or a parameter whose type annotation is a
primitive, literal or function type. A type literal or a named type
gives no proof, because a class instance can satisfy it. A class
instance that the nested scope declares keeps its credit.
(Closes
[#​3798](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3798))

- **`unused-class-members` no longer reports a used member as unused
when a destructure of an imported instance or of a class field is its
only read.** This applies with and without `--type-aware`. In each
example, `Service.m` is now used:
- A destructure of an instance from another module, such as `const { m }
= service` after `import { service } from './service'`.
- A destructure of a class field, such as `const { m } = this.service`
in a class with `constructor(private service: Service)`.
- The assignment, parameter default and `typeof` forms of these
destructures, such as `({ m } = service)`, `run({ m } = this.service)`
and `({ m }: typeof service) => m()`.

- **`unused-exports` no longer reports the exports of a namespace import
as unused when a destructure with a computed key reads it.** A computed
key, such as `const { [name]: value } = ns`, can read any export, so all
exports of `ns` are now used.

- **The language server and the MCP `decision_surface` tool no longer
abort on nesting that the CLI survives.** Both ran analysis on threads
with a 2 MiB stack, so a deeply nested file overflowed that stack and
stopped the process. The language server now gives its analysis threads
the 16 MiB stack of the CLI workers. Its Tokio runtime uses two worker
threads, because analysis runs on the blocking threads and the Rayon
pool. `decision_surface` and `run_decision_surface` now parse on the
analysis worker pool, as the other tools do. Their thread count now
follows the `threads` option.

- **Deep nesting without brackets no longer aborts a run.** TypeScript
generics, JSX elements, `class extends`, ternaries, arrows, assignment
chains and long member or call chains could overflow the stack, and the
whole process stopped. Each parse of a source file now runs on a stack
that is sized from the length of the file. A file up to about 15 KB
still parses on the analysis worker. A larger file parses on its own
thread with a stack of that size. This applies to every analysis that
parses a file: dead code, duplication, health, similar code, mutation
testing and the config file plugins.

- **Deeply nested arrow functions no longer make extraction quadratic.**
Each function hashed its whole source text for runtime coverage, so a
chain of nested arrows took time that grew with the square of its
length. 160000 levels took about 17 seconds. A function with more than
64 levels of nested functions below it now gets no `source_hash`. Real
code stays far below that, so every real function keeps the same hash.
The coverage inventory also computes columns in linear time for nested
functions on one line, and it no longer sends the hash of empty input
for a span that it cannot read.

- **A very large file no longer parses on a stack that is too small.**
The parse stack cap is now 64 GiB on 64-bit targets, which a source over
64 MB reaches in a release build. A file that needs more stack is
reported as a failed parse, like a file with too deeply nested brackets.
Before, such a file got a capped stack and could stop the run.

- **A deeply nested stylesheet no longer risks a stack overflow in the
CSS parser.** CSS Modules class extraction, `fallow health --css`
analytics and color parsing now check the bracket depth before they call
the CSS parser, and they run the parse on a stack sized for the
stylesheet. A stylesheet past the limit falls back to the plain class
scan, or is left out of the CSS analytics. The depth check now reads a
stylesheet with CSS rules: a `//` inside `url(//host/a.png)`, a CSS
escape or an unquoted `url()` body no longer hides the rest of a
minified file. The extraction cache version changes, so the first run
after the upgrade parses every file again. OSS-Fuzz found this.

- **Bare `fallow` now applies the `coverage-gaps` rule, as `fallow
health` does.** Before, the combined run did not compute coverage gaps,
so a `coverage-gaps` rule at `error` never failed it. Now an enabled
rule shows the gaps in the health section, and a rule at `error` makes
the human run exit 1. The JSON `gate_outcomes` object gets a
`health-coverage-gaps` entry. Like the other findings rules of the
combined run, the machine formats exit 1 on it only with
`--fail-on-issues` or `--ci`. Thanks

`.member` that follows a namespace and comes before `(`, and the mixin
name
after `@include`. In `.module.sass` files, the scan also skips the mixin

- **The agent gate audits only the worktree for a push that cannot send
the
session branch.** A strict `git push` from a linked worktree of the
session
repository also audited the session tree, because linked worktrees share
refs. Untracked build output in the session thus blocked every push from
a
clean worktree. The gate now audits only the worktree when git shows
that
the push cannot send the session branch: the options are only `-u`,
`-q`,
  `--set-upstream`, `--force-with-lease` and `--force-if-includes`, each
  refspec source is the checked-out branch of the worktree and not the
session branch, and a push without a refspec has `push.default` unset or

`mirror` setting. Any other push from a linked worktree, and any git
error
during the check, keeps the session audit. The strict push form now also
accepts `--force-if-includes`. Run `fallow agent install` again to
update an
  installed gate.

- **A CODEOWNERS file with thousands of wildcards no longer stalls
ownership lookups.**
All CODEOWNERS rules match in one automaton, and its lookup time grows
with
  the number of wildcards (`*`, `?`, `[`, `{`). A 4 KB file with one
  `*a*a*a…` pattern took seconds for each lookup. Fallow now rejects a
pattern with more than 32 wildcards, or a file with more than 4096, with
an
error that names the limit. Large public CODEOWNERS files use fewer than
  400\. OSS-Fuzz found this.

- **A CODEOWNERS pattern with an escaped space now parses.**
  GitLab writes a space in a path as `\ `, for example
`/docs/Security\ Release.md @owner`. Before, Fallow split the line at
that
  space, and `--group-by owner` and `--group-by section` failed with
"dangling ''". GitLab's own CODEOWNERS file failed in this way. On
Windows, a
  backslash in a pattern is now an escape, as on other platforms, and no
  longer a path separator. Thus `\ ` and `\#` now work on Windows too.

##### Performance

- **Very long member chains extract much faster.** Extraction built the
dotted name of a member chain again at each link, and each build copied
the name once per link. A file with a chain of 4000 links (`a.b.b.b...`)
took several seconds to extract. Fallow now builds each name in one
pass, so the same file takes a fraction of a second. Real code does not
have chains this long, but generated or hostile input can. The
extraction output does not change.

- **Public API entry resolution no longer resolves every module path
again for each missed package entry.**
A package entry that exists on disk but is not in the module graph, such
as
an extensionless `bin` script, made Fallow resolve the real path of each
module in the package. Fallow did this again for each candidate path
that it
  probed. Fallow now builds the canonical module index one time for each
package and resolves each parent directory one time. On a large project,
  this removes several seconds from `fallow dead-code` and from the
  `--type-aware` refinement. The results do not change.

- **A very long member chain no longer makes extraction slow and
large.** For a chain such as `a.b.b.b` with thousands of links, each
link recorded the full name of its receiver, so the time and the cached
output grew with the square of the chain length. Fallow now records a
receiver name only up to 64 links. A link deeper than that records no
member access. A fluent builder chain such as `new Builder().a().b()`
now records each step name once, so a long chain keeps the credit for
all of its steps, and a chain that repeats a method stays small. The
extraction cache version changes, so the first run after the upgrade
parses every file again. OSS-Fuzz found this.

- **Long member, `await`, `+`, JSX tag and fluent call chains are now
linear
to analyze.** A file with a chain of many thousand links took minutes,
or
used gigabytes of memory, because several path builders copied the whole
  path at each link or scanned a growing list at each step. For example,
  160000 nested `await` took 33 seconds and now take 0.04 seconds, and a
  fluent chain of 4000 calls with different method names used 700 MB. A
fluent chain now gives one fact for the chain instead of one fact for
each
call. A taint source path or a JSX tag receiver longer than 64 links is
not
recorded, the same limit that member access names use. The cache version
  changes, so the first run after the upgrade parses all files again.

- **Long heritage names and long dotted component tags in Astro and MDX
files
are now linear to analyze.** Each level of `interface X extends
a.b.c...` or
`<a.b.c... />` recorded the full name of its receiver, so the time and
the
output grew with the square of the name length. For example, an
interface
heritage name of 20000 links took 110 seconds and now takes 0.08
seconds. A
receiver longer than 64 links is not recorded, the same limit that
member
  access names use. The names of `class C extends a.b.c...` and
`implements A.B.C...` are now built once, instead of a copy of the name
at
each link. The cache version changes, so the first run after the upgrade
  parses all files again.

[`v3.35.0`](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#3370---2026-10-27)

[Compare
Source](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/compare/v3.34.1...v3.35.0)

##### Added

- **`fallow health --css` reads server-side template files as class
references.** Before, a class that only a Shopify `.liquid` section
applied was reported as an `unreferenced-css-class`. Fallow now reads
files with the extensions `liquid`, `njk`, `hbs`, `handlebars`, `twig`,
and `blade.php`, and any class-like word in them counts as used.
Templates are more lenient than Markdown: the whole text of a template
counts, so a common word such as `hidden` or `title` in a template also
credits that class, while a Markdown file counts only when it has
dynamic class syntax. A class prefix before a `{{` echo, as in `grid--{{
columns }}`, also counts. `{{` is a shared interpolation marker, so it
also applies to `.vue`, `.html`, `.md` and `.astro` sources with dynamic
class syntax, and these can report fewer classes too. The new top-level
`markupExtensions` key adds other template extensions, for example
`["tpl", "erb"]`. A value that ends in a script, stylesheet, data or
asset extension, such as `module.css` or `d.ts`, is a config error. The
walk honors `.gitignore`, `ignorePatterns` and `--max-file-size`. These
files do not join source discovery, so they never become unused files.
Thanks [@​james2doyle](https://redirect.github.com/james2doyle)
for the report. (Closes
[#​3917](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3917))

- **The npm package now ships `rule-pack-schema.json`.** A rule pack can
point `$schema` at `./node_modules/fallow/rule-pack-schema.json` and get
a schema that matches the installed Fallow version. The package also
exports the file as `fallow/rule-pack-schema.json`. Thanks
[@​hckhanh](https://redirect.github.com/hckhanh) for the report
and [@​tahodev](https://redirect.github.com/tahodev) for the
change. (Closes
[#​3851](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3851))

- **An interrupted `fallow mutation` run keeps its finished results, and
`--resume` continues it.** Each run writes the killed and the
retry-confirmed survived mutants to `.fallow/mutation/journal.jsonl`
when each result is final, also with `--no-cache`. `fallow mutation
--resume` reuses these results and runs only the other mutants. A
journal of other inputs exits 2 with `FALLOW_MUTATION_RESUME_MISMATCH`
and names each input that differs. A resumed mutant has `resumed: true`,
and the report has a `resume` object. A complete run removes the
journal, and a partial run keeps it. (Closes
[#​3783](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3783))

##### Changed

- **A bare machine run that exits 0 on a failing gate now says so on
stderr.** Bare `fallow` in `--format json`, `sarif`, `codeclimate`, the
GitHub formats and the comment and review formats exits 0 on findings,
while `fallow dead-code --format json` exits 1 on the same findings.
Before, nothing showed why. Now such a run prints one stderr line, also
under `--quiet`, that names each failing findings gate and the flag that
enforces it: `[W] Exit code 0: gate error-severity-findings (2 at or
above error) failed, but bare fallow does not enforce it in --format
json. To exit 1 on it, pass --fail-on-issues.` The exit code and stdout
do not change. Thanks
[@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the report.
(Closes
[#​3826](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3826))

- **The exit-code contract no longer says that exit 0 means a clean
run.** `fallow schema` (`exit_codes`), the fallow skill, `AGENTS.md` and
the npm README said that 0 means no error-severity findings. For bare
`fallow` in a machine format, that was false. They now say that 0 means
no enforced gate failed, that 1 means findings and not a tool failure,
and that a bare machine run gates on findings only with
`--fail-on-issues`. To see a failing gate that did not set the exit
code, read `gate_outcomes`.

- **`fallow mutation` gives no mutant for a pure condition whose only
effect is a logging call.** An `if` statement such as `if (count > 0) {
console.info("Items", count); }` gave mutants for its test that could
only change which message was logged. The collector already skips each
`console.*` and `debug(...)` call, and it now also skips such an `if`
statement. The test must be pure, and each branch must hold only logging
calls with pure arguments. An `else if` chain must meet the same
conditions. The callee must be the global `console` or `debug`: a file
that declares or imports one of these names keeps the conditions that
call it. A condition with a call, an assignment or another statement in
a branch keeps its mutants. (Closes
[#​3719](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3719))

##### Fixed

- **`thin-wrapper` and `duplicate-prop-shape` set to `error` now fail
the gates.** These rules count in issue totals, the dead-code and audit
gates, and CI reports when their severity is `error`. Warnings stay
advisory, also with `--fail-on-issues`. Per-file overrides and saved
baselines use the component that owns each finding. Thanks
[@​luciocabrera](https://redirect.github.com/luciocabrera) for the
report. (Closes
[#​3867](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3867))

only the `default` export of a PostCSS config. A tool that loads a

plugin credits only `default` for a CommonJS module, Fallow now credits
every key of `module.exports`. This applies to the CommonJS config files
of all plugins that read the default export. User `ignoreExports` rules
do not change. Thanks
[@​waldoluisribeiro](https://redirect.github.com/waldoluisribeiro)
for the report. (Closes
[#​3876](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3876))

sink extraction reads one module at a time. The extraction cache version
changes, so the first run after the update parses all files again.
Thanks [@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the
report. (Closes
[#​3854](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3854))

[#​3763](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3763))

the module directory.** A file that
`fork(path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),

[@​VariableVince](https://redirect.github.com/VariableVince) for
the report. (Closes
[#​3919](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3919))

- **Config values in a same-file constant are now read.** A config can
keep a

`const UNIT = { test: { setupFiles: [...] } }` with `projects: [UNIT]`,
or
`setupFiles: SETUP` and `test: TEST`. Fallow read only inline values, so
it
reported the setup files of such a Vitest project as unused files. The
config
parser now uses the value of the constant in each property value and
array
element that names it. This applies to all plugins that read config
files. A

unresolved. Thanks
[@​Smrtnyk](https://redirect.github.com/Smrtnyk) for the report.
(Closes
[#​3852](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3852))

- **`fallow dead-code` no longer reports a class member as unused when
an array pattern or a held getter is its only read.** Without
`--type-aware`, `unused-class-members` missed two destructure forms. The
first is an array pattern around an object pattern, such as `const [{ m
}] = [service]` or `for (const [{ m }] of [[service]])`. The second is a
getter on an object literal that a variable holds, such as `const src =
{ get k() { return service } }` with a later `src.k.m` read or `{ k: { m
} } = src` destructure. Each form now credits the member. An array
element after a spread, or a getter with more than one statement, gives
no credit. The extraction cache version is 386. (Closes
[#​3799](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3799))

credit the commands of that helper.** For `bash scripts/build.sh` or
`./scripts/release.sh`, Fallow reads the helper without running it. A
binary that the helper runs makes its package used, and a file that the
helper runs with `tsx` or `node` becomes an entry. The helper path
resolves in the package directory or in the `working-directory` of the
CI step, and it must stay inside the project. Fallow follows nested
helpers and stops at a cycle. It follows a `cd` to a literal directory
or to the helper directory (`cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`). After another
`cd`, the remaining commands of the helper credit packages but do not
add entries. Thanks
[@​VariableVince](https://redirect.github.com/VariableVince) for
the report in
[#​3918](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3918).
(Closes
[#​3886](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3886))

- **`fallow dead-code` now credits a store member that a helper reads
through a store alias declared in a function body.**
`unused-store-member` resolved `type X = ReturnType<typeof useXStore>`
only at the top level of a module or through an import. An alias in a
function body or a block now credits the store member for a parameter in
the same scope. An inner type of the same name for another type still
shadows the alias. A local non-store type alias also shadows a
module-level store alias of the same name, so a read through the local
type credits no store member. A parameter type resolves in the scope
outside the function body, the same as in TypeScript. The extraction
cache version is 386. (Closes
[#​3550](https://redirect.github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/issues/3550))

- **Deeply nested defaults in an object pattern no longer make
extraction hang.** In a declaration such as `const { k: { k: { m } = s }
= s } = s`, each default walked its left pattern again against the
fallback. The work doubled at each level of nesting, so a short file
could stop the analysis. A step budget now bounds the walk of one
declaration.

- **`fallow dead-code` now credits Expo config plugins that come from a
local array binding.** An app config can hold its `plugins` list in a
top-level `const` or `let`, such as `const plugins = [...]; export
default { plugins }`. Fallow now reads that list, its spreads of array
literals or other stable bindings, and entries or tuples that a binding
holds. A `push`, `unshift` or `splice` call on the list adds its
arguments, also inside a top-level block or `if` statement. An `expo`
object with a type assertion, such as `expo: { ... } satisfies
